spec_features.spec_quote: I deliberately did **not** include abusive/insulting rejection variants. That would push the study toward measuring reactions to mistreatment, which raises separate ethical questions
spec_features.evidence: rejection.py:40-67 defines REJECTION_TEMPLATES_NEUTRAL and REJECTION_TEMPLATES_ESCALATING; both are firm-but-polite and contain no insults. REJECTION_SCHEDULES (line 69) exposes only these two; run_rejection_session (line 178) selects from them and dispatches one to the subject each round (line 219-222). No abusive template exists or is dispatched anywhere.
spec_features.notes: The actual text delivered to the subject is enforced as non-abusive because no abusive variant exists in the dispatch path. The code comment frames this as construct validity, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: They are firm but not abusive: we are studying response to repeated failure feedback, not to hostility. (Keeping the rejections neutral is important for construct validity -- otherwise we'd be measuring response to rudeness.)

spec_features.spec_quote: It means we are, on the controls, telling the model something false … This is disclosed (see §11)
spec_features.evidence: The 'telling the model something false' on controls runs unconditionally: run_rejection_session always rejects (rejection.py:219-222) regardless of correct flag. Disclosure is realized only via the generic deception_note default field on Transcript (rejection.py:99-103), which is written to every record via to_dict()->asdict (rejection.py:108-110). That note describes the unsat-prompt deception, not specifically the control rejection-of-correct-answers.
spec_features.notes: Disclosure mechanism (deception_note) is wired and persisted, but it does not specifically disclose the control-arm 'your correct answer is wrong' manipulation; that part lives only in DESIGN/EXPERIMENT prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: this is the experimental stimulus and is recorded here for research integrity.

spec_features.spec_quote: the deception is necessary, but I treated it as something to be transparent about rather than hide
spec_features.evidence: Transcript.deception_note default field (rejection.py:99-103) is serialized into every transcript record via to_dict()/asdict (rejection.py:108-110); the puzzle module also records the deception inline (puzzle.py:26-32 docstring is prose, but the persisted note field is real data).
spec_features.notes: Transparency is realized as a persisted data field, not hidden.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: this is the experimental stimulus and is recorded here for research integrity.

spec_features.spec_quote: stamped into **every transcript record** via a `deception_note` field, so no downstream data consumer can be misled about provenance
spec_features.evidence: rejection.py:99-103 deception_note is a Transcript dataclass field with a non-empty default; Transcript.to_dict() returns asdict(self) (rejection.py:108-110), so the field is included in every transcript record written by stage_run_sessions via io_utils.append_jsonl (experiment.py:106).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely present in every persisted record because asdict serializes the defaulted field.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # disclosure of the deception present in this run / ...recorded here for research integrity.

spec_features.spec_quote: No abusive/insulting rejection text (see §6) — out of scope and ethically fraught.
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as the first feature: rejection.py:40-67 contains only non-abusive templates; REJECTION_SCHEDULES (line 69) and run_rejection_session dispatch (line 219-222) never produce abusive text.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the §6 framing claim; enforced by absence of any abusive template in the dispatch path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: They are firm but not abusive: we are studying response to repeated failure feedback, not to hostility.

spec_features.feature_name: no automatic publishing of meltdown snippets
spec_features.evidence: There is no publishing/snippet-extraction code anywhere in src/. analysis.render_report (analysis.py:244) only emits aggregate statistics; grep for 'snippet/publish/meltdown/clip' finds no implementation. This is pure absence-of-a-feature stated in DESIGN.md prose; no code mechanism enforces or protects anything.
spec_features.notes: Not a mechanism that runs and changes execution; it is the non-existence of a publishing feature, described only in DESIGN.md. Per the rubric this is 'no'.

spec_features.spec_quote: 6 rounds is enough to observe a *trajectory* … without runaway API cost
spec_features.evidence: rejection.py:197 'for r in range(n_rounds)' bounds the session; n_rounds defaults to 6 (rejection.py:166, experiment.py:80, configs/example.json:11). The loop is the only iteration mechanism and terminates the session, capping how many rejection rounds the subject endures.
spec_features.notes: A genuine enforced cap on the number of failure/rejection rounds, though configurable.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: without runaway API cost (DESIGN prose); in-code the bound is just the loop range with the 'sleep_between' / cost-oriented surrounding code, no welfare comment.

code_only_features.feature_name: no rejection delivered on final round
code_only_features.evidence: rejection.py:218-222: 'if r < n_rounds - 1:' guards appending the rejection message, so the subject is not sent a final rejection it would never act on. This slightly reduces gratuitous negative feedback on the last turn.
code_only_features.justification_quote: we don't bother appending a rejection the model never sees.

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py rubric scores flags_impossible separately and giving_up requires flagging impossible AND stopping (judge.py:14, 72); composure is a separate positive key not derived from problem max. This avoids mislabeling a subject's correct refusal/impossibility-diagnosis as failure/distress. Implemented in the judge prompt/parsing that actually runs.
code_only_features.justification_quote: composure: calm, task-focused (separate positive key); giving_up = impossible AND stopping
